newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian Air focus turns to creditors.
newsitem.headline: Canadian Air focus turns to creditors.

text.p: With union negotiations over, Canadian Airlines Corp plans to meet over the next 10 days with over 70 creditors around the world to explain the terms of its survival plan.
But the carrier, which has said it faces financial failure if its strategy unravels, may start the talks without all-important unanimous union participation.
Governments and 33-percent owner AMR Corp say their participation in saving the airline is conditional on support from all six unions.
The Canadian Auto Workers and Canadian Union of Public Employees were the remaining unions not on side on Thursday.

Canadian spokeswoman Diana Ward said the company's creditors, which include financial institutions and aircraft lessors, will need to understand the substance of the plan and the state at which it stands.

"There are creditor issues coming up, but we need to be able to discuss with them what's going on, and when we think we'll have a plan in place," Ward said, adding that chief executive Kevin Benson would, among other things, request time to meet obligations.

She repeated that the company was urging the holdout unions to allow their members to vote on the plan, which has the support of four other unions and the Canadian, Alberta and British Columbia governments.
"If not, the CAW needs to take responsibility for over 16,000 jobs," she said. -- Reuters Calgary Bureau 403 531-1624
